title: Beyond Bolted-On Screen Readers: Narrative Phenomenology, the RNIB Roundhouse Sensory Dark, and Perceptual-Cognitive Unity (Rasa-Darśan)
author: Borealis Serenity Hedling
acknowledgement: Special thanks to Flyxion (@standardgalactic) for pioneering the research-projection direction that surfaced spoken-word AI failure modes.
limitations: Neural VITS speech models still approximate—rather than replace—a live human narrator.
Replacing 2D spatial navigation with discrete gestures trades open-world exploration freedom for narrative coherence.

turns.speaker: Speaker A
turns.text: Imagine stepping into a darkened room with no visual screen at all. Instead of a robot reading pixel coordinates in your ear, you hear a mountain river flowing gently through a low-pass filter.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.text: Under the Social Model of Disability, bolting an aria-live distance counter onto a visual grid grants navigational permission, yet leaves blind listeners doing mental trigonometry instead of inhabiting rasa-darśan.

turns.speaker: Speaker A
turns.text: Inspired by RNIB and Roundhouse sensory-darkness storytelling and research-projection experiments by Flyxion, every gesture—like chiming a Tōrō lantern or Bonshō bell—produces the sound, voice, and reflection together.

turns.speaker: Speaker B
turns.text: Even with warmer neural voices, we must state clear limits: VITS models only approximate human breath, and discrete gestures narrow spatial freedom. Naming those boundaries keeps the work honest.
